reasons: The rule is genuinely triggered: the Agreement skips from Section 19 (Warranties) to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability) and the only indemnity references are incidental cross-references (9.3's 'remedies required by Section 20.5', 19.5, 21.3's Excluded Claims), so Vendor owes no defence or indemnity — a critical missing-clause deviation.

The inserted article reaches the preferred position: Vendor defence/indemnity for third-party IP infringement, Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents, and Vendor's gross negligence/wilful misconduct, plus standard notice/control/cooperation procedure and a Customer indemnity narrowed to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Placement and numbering are correct and repair the dangling cross-references: the new article slots into the vacant Section 20 between Warranties and Limitation of Liability, with exclusions at 20.4 and infringement remedies (procure/modify/replace/refund) at 20.5 so Section 9.3's reference resolves, and 21.3's Excluded Claims carve-out becomes operative.
Comment is accurate, correctly cites the playbook position, and offers a sensible fallback (accept usual exclusions; discuss a super-cap) without over-conceding; tone and prefix conform.

Minor, non-blocking drafting nits: the inserted text uses 'Affiliates', 'Customer Data', and 'Vendor Technology' as capitalised terms that are not among the resolved definitions supplied, and the heading is rendered without the '20.' number — worth confirming these terms are defined in the Agreement's definitions article before sending.
